**Dependence Analysis:**
The inner loop copies `a[0]` to all array elements. The blocking dependence occurs because iteration i=0 writes to `a[0]` (even though it writes back what it read), while iterations i>0 read from `a[0]`. This creates a loop-carried RAW dependence.

**Key Insight:**
Iteration 0 writes the same value to `a[0]` that it reads (a no-op), so the actual value of `a[0]` doesn't change during the loop. All iterations semantically read the initial value of `a[0]`.

**Solution:**
Capture `a[0]` into a temporary variable before the loop, then replace the read of `a[0]` with the temporary. This removes the loop-carried dependence since all iterations now read from a constant (the temporary) rather than the shared array element. The inner loop has ~32,000 iterations per activation—sufficient work to justify parallelization.
